papers.title_en: Context-aware Attention-based Gaussian Mixture Models for Vehicular Trajectory Prediction
papers.authors: Arash Raftari, Babak Ebrahimi Soorchaei, Yaser P. Fallah
papers.evidence: 面向车辆轨迹预测的上下文感知注意力高斯混合模型
papers.tldr: 面向协同与自动驾驶的可靠可解释轨迹预测，在复杂不确定环境中仍具挑战。本文提出 CAA-GMM，将未来运动建模为场景上下文与智能体动力学共同条件化的概率混合，并用轻量注意力融合交互与环境线索。在 nuScenes 和 Argoverse 2 上，该方法精度媲美或超越栅格基线，且计算复杂度低，消融验证注意力模块作用。在通信与感知不完美条件下也展现韧性，为智能交通协同预测提供高效可扩展方案。
papers.abstract_en: Reliable and interpretable trajectory prediction is critical for cooperative and autonomous driving in complex and uncertain environments. This paper introduces a Context-Aware Attention-based Gaussian Mixture Model (CAA-GMM) for multimodal, uncertainty-aware motion forecasting. The proposed approach models future motion as a probabilistic mixture conditioned on both scene context and agent dynamics, capturing diverse behavioral modes with interpretable Gaussian components. A lightweight attention mechanism adaptively encodes inter-agent interactions and contextual salience, enabling efficient fusion of rasterized environment cues and motion history in dense traffic scenes. Comprehensive evaluations on the nuScenes and Argoverse 2 datasets demonstrate that CAA-GMM achieves competitive or superior accuracy compared with state-of-the-art raster-based baselines, while maintaining low computational complexity. Ablation analyses confirm the importance of the attention module for robust contextual reasoning and predictive precision. Furthermore, evaluations under imperfect communication and perception conditions highlight the framework's resilience to uncertainty, establishing CAA-GMM as an efficient and scalable solution for cooperative trajectory prediction in intelligent transportation systems.

papers.title_en: Not All Uncertainty Matters: Simulation-in-the-Loop Fast-Slow Reasoning for Decision-Critical Autonomous Driving System
papers.authors: Jiayi Chen, Shuai Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Chengzhong Xu, Kaibin Huang
papers.evidence: 面向决策关键自动驾驶的VLM快慢推理
papers.tldr: 大VLM为自动驾驶提供开放世界推理，但云端计算与延迟高，难以持续使用，快慢协作需判断何时云推理真正影响实时决策。SIGMA将规划器嵌入不确定性评估，通过仿真分析语义与几何不确定性下的场景实现如何改变可行轨迹与规划代价，并定义EPG指标用于云调用、引导集成与请求优先级。CARLA实验中，不必要云交互减少50%，导航成功率提升超6%，动态场景完成时间最多降26.2%。该工作以决策收益而非不确定性本身触发云推理，提升任务导向快慢协作效率。
papers.abstract_en: Large vision-language models (VLMs) provide powerful open-world perception and reasoning for autonomous driving, but their high computational cost and inference latency make continuous cloud-side use impractical. This motivates fast--slow collaboration, where efficient onboard modules handle real-time perception and control while cloud models provide high-level reasoning only when needed. The key challenge is deciding when cloud reasoning should influence time-critical driving decisions. Existing methods often rely on perception uncertainty, heuristic triggers, or resource-driven policies, without assessing whether resolving an uncertainty will improve planning. We propose \textbf{SIGMA}, a simulation-in-the-loop framework for task-oriented fast--slow collaboration. SIGMA embeds the planner into uncertainty assessment and evaluates how plausible scene realizations under semantic and geometric uncertainty affect feasible trajectories and planning cost. Based on these outcomes, it estimates the expected reduction in planning cost from resolving uncertainty. We further introduce expected planning gain (EPG), a decision-level metric for cloud invocation, cloud-guidance integration, and request prioritization under deadline and resource constraints. Experiments in CARLA show that SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions while improving planning, efficiency, and navigation success in static and dynamic obstacle scenarios. Compared with fixed-period collaboration, SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions by 50\%, improves navigation success by more than 6\%, and cuts finish time by up to 26.2\% in dynamic scenarios.

papers.title_en: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
papers.authors: Zihao Zhang, Haochen Tian, Tianyu Li, Changhui Jing, Jingliang He, Naisheng Ye, Ziyuan Pu, Zhenjie Yang
papers.evidence: 面向端到端自动驾驶的规划器无关视觉表征对齐
papers.tldr: 视觉基础模型（VFMs）被大量引入端到端自动驾驶，但其表征何时真正提升驾驶性能仍不明确。为此提出与规划器无关的视觉表征对齐框架ViRA，在不改变规划器结构与推理开销的前提下开展系统研究。结果显示VFM对齐可稳定提升多种端到端规划器性能并延伸至零样本闭环，辅助感知监督还能把五个VFM目标间的EPDMS差距从2.7分收窄至0.5分。据此构建的ViRA-Diffusion在NAVSIM v2 navtest上取得92.3 EPDMS，领先对比方法至少1.9分。
papers.abstract_en: Visual foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly integrated into end-to-end autonomous driving for their powerful representations, yet it remains unclear when these representations improve driving performance. To investigate this question, we introduce ViRA, a planner-agnostic visual representation alignment framework that keeps the planner architecture and inference cost unchanged. Our study reveals three findings: (1) VFM-guided visual representations consistently improve driving performance across diverse end-to-end planners, with gains extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation. (2) The choice of VFM target matters for planning performance, and alignment to a different VFM can further benefit planners with pre-trained VFM encoders. (3) Auxiliary perception supervision reduces sensitivity to VFM target selection, narrowing the EPDMS spread across five targets from 2.7 to 0.5 points and potentially compensating for less effective VFM targets. Guided by these findings, we develop ViRA-Diffusion, a diffusion-based planner trained without auxiliary perception supervision, which achieves 92.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest, outperforming recent methods in our comparison by at least 1.9 points. The results motivate jointly considering target selection and planner supervision when integrating VFMs into end-to-end autonomous driving. The results and demo are available at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/ViRA.

papers.title_en: ΔWAM: Distilling Action Tangent Fields into World Action Models
papers.authors: Ke Wu, Hanwen Huang, Bo Gu, Kaizhao Zhang, Xiangting Meng, Yupeng Zheng, Zijun Xu, Jieru Zhao, Wenchao Ding
papers.evidence: 将动作相关动态蒸馏进机器人世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 世界动作模型用稠密未来预测增强稀疏动作监督，但未来中大量是可从外观预测的场景持续性，动作相关变化占比低。本文提出动作切向场，用动作条件世界模型在 Residual-VAE 空间探测动作扰动与未来残差的一阶局部对应，并将其蒸馏进 WAM 去噪监督。方法在 LIBERO-Plus、RoboTwin、RoboTwin2.0-Plus 上提升对光照、背景、相机、布局等扰动的鲁棒性，且无需大规模具身预训练，并将多步 VideoDiT 去噪蒸馏为单步推理。这表明有效 WAM 监督应信息丰富且聚焦动作改变未来的方向。
papers.abstract_en: World Action Models (WAM) improve robot policies by augmenting sparse action supervision with dense future prediction. However, much of the predictable future is dominated by appearance and scene persistence rather than action-dependent dynamics. We observe that several recent WAM designs, including optical flow, motion-centric representations, and latent actions, can be understood from a common perspective in which world supervision becomes more efficient as it contains a higher proportion of action-relevant variation. Based on this insight, we introduce Action Tangent Fields, which reformulate world supervision through a local Taylor expansion of how actions induce changes in future dynamics. We represent future dynamics in Residual-VAE space, where the future latent remains recoverable from the current latent and its residual, and use a strong action-conditioned world model (ACWM) to probe the local correspondence between action variations and residual-world variations. This local first-order structure is distilled into the WAM to guide its denoising supervision toward dynamics that are more tightly coupled to action, rather than merely predictable from appearance. Across LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin, and RoboTwin2.0-Plus, our method consistently improves robustness to lighting, background, camera, layout, and other environmental perturbations. Despite using no large-scale embodied pretraining, it achieves stronger robustness under several distribution shifts than pretrained policies. We further distill multi-step VideoDiT denoising into a single step for efficient inference. Our results suggest that effective WAM supervision should remain information-rich while concentrating its predictive capacity on the directions along which actions change the future.

papers.title_en: AffordDrive3D: Affordance-Aware World-Action Modeling with Spatial Understanding
papers.authors: Tianhui Cai, Xinglong Sun, Chao Fang, Zhenxin Li, Rui Song, Jose M. Alvarez, Yunxiang Mao, Jiaqi Ma, Langechuan Liu
papers.evidence: 面向驾驶轨迹生成的可供性感知世界-动作建模
papers.tldr: 现有世界-动作模型多依赖RGB外观预测未来，近期引入几何虽增强空间理解，但稠密几何未指出哪些区域与自车动作相关。为此提出AffordDrive3D，以VLM为骨干联合预测可行驶区域与碰撞关键区域，并从RGB世界模型隐变量预测未来几何。在NAVSIM上取得91.3 PDMS与89.9 EPDMS的SOTA，验证了联合建模未来可供性与几何对轨迹规划的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: World-action models have recently improved autonomous driving by jointly learning future scene prediction and trajectory generation. Most existing approaches model the future primarily through RGB appearance, and recent works have begun to incorporate geometric prediction to improve spatial understanding. However, dense geometry describes the spatial layout of the entire scene without indicating which parts are most relevant to the ego vehicle's action. For driving, the model must also identify and anticipate where it can safely move and which regions may pose collision risks. Jointly modeling action-relevant regions and future geometry can provide the policy with both driving-relevant cues and their corresponding spatial structure. We therefore propose AffordDrive3D, an affordance- and geometry-aware world-action model that jointly learns future action-relevant regions and spatial structure. In order to capture the scene semantics and driving context needed for driving affordance prediction, we build AffordDrive3D on a VLM backbone to forecast drivable areas and collision-critical regions that directly affect ego motion, while predicting future geometry from RGB world-model latents. On NAVSIM, AffordDrive3D achieves state-of-the-art performance with 91.3 PDMS and 89.9 EPDMS, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly modeling future affordances and geometry for trajectory planning. Project Page: https://afforddrive3d.github.io/

papers.title_en: VGGTWorld-VLA: Intent-Conditioned 3D World Evolution for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Zhaoyang Liu, Kun Jiang, Ziying Song, Diange Yang
papers.evidence: 面向驾驶的意图条件化3D世界演化与未来预测
papers.tldr: 现有基于VGGT的几何世界模型能从视觉观测恢复统一3D场景，但未来演化对驾驶意图与动作条件较弱，难以预测不同自车动作下的备选未来。提出VGGTWorld-VLA，以动作-语义条件机制将驾驶语义和自车运动注入未来token流，并用几何-语言-动作桥接联合历史几何、VLA语义及机动轨迹表示进行条件建模。NAVSIM上，方法未来几何预测性能与基线相比具竞争力，消融验证语义与动作条件的有效性。该工作展示了可控VGGT世界演化在自动驾驶中的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: VGGT provides a strong foundation for geometry-centric world models by recovering unified 3D scene geometry from visual observations. Although recent extensions enable temporal 3D prediction, their future evolution remains weakly conditioned on driving intentions and actions, limiting their ability to model alternative action-dependent futures. We propose VGGTWorld-VLA, an intention-conditioned extension of VGGT-World for controllable 3D world evolution in autonomous driving. First, we introduce an action--semantic conditioning mechanism that injects complementary driving semantics and ego-motion representations into the future-token stream, enabling different future geometry predictions for the same observed scene under alternative ego actions. Second, we develop a geometry--language--action bridge that adapts historical geometry, VLA semantic features, and maneuver and trajectory representations for joint conditioning of future geometry prediction. We evaluate future geometry prediction on NAVSIM, while conditioning ablations further examine the contributions of semantic and action information. Compared with the baseline, our method demonstrates competitive geometry prediction performance. Ablation studies further support the effectiveness of semantic and action conditioning. These results demonstrate the potential of semantic and action conditioning for controllable VGGT-based world prediction in autonomous driving.

papers.title_en: PlanWAM: Planning-Shaped Future Representations for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Jinchang Xu, Hongda Yu, Fengwei Dong, Wenhui Huang, Xi Wei, Yongzhi Liu, Sunan Zhang, Jirao Wang, Chen Lv, Bingbing Li, Guodong Yin, Weichao Zhuang
papers.evidence: 面向端到端自动驾驶的规划塑形世界-动作模型
papers.tldr: 端到端自动驾驶的世界模型可预测未来以辅助规划，但较少探究哪种未来表征最利于规划。PlanWAM提出规划塑形世界动作模型，用规划任务塑造未来隐表征，并通过时序寄存器金字塔与事后到前瞻蒸馏，让仅依赖历史的先验分支预测该表征，作为规划上下文引导轨迹生成与选择。在NAVSIM-v1/v2上取得93.8 PDMS/90.9 EPDMS，HUGSIM零样本闭环达38.7 HD-Score。大量实验结果表明规划塑形未来表征是有效且可部署的前瞻形式。
papers.abstract_en: World models in end-to-end autonomous driving predict future scene evolution to provide foresight for trajectory planning. Existing methods mainly study how to predict the future and how to use it, but less often ask which future representation is actually most useful for planning. To this end, we propose PlanWAM, a Planning-Shaped World Action Model. The key idea is to let the planning task shape the future-state representation, so that it retains the information most useful for planning. A latent world model then predicts this planning-shaped future latent representation from historical observations and uses it for planning, enabling foresighted planning. Specifically, we first use a Temporal Register Pyramid to compress multi-frame historical information in a recency-aware manner, learning a compact history representation oriented toward future reasoning and planning. We then introduce a privileged future posterior branch that observes ground-truth future frames, and shape its future latent representation with trajectory-planning objectives to obtain a planning-shaped future latent representation. Hindsight-to-Foresight Distillation trains a prior branch that depends only on history to predict this future latent representation. The predicted future latent representation serves as planning context and guides trajectory generation and selection. PlanWAM achieves 93.8 PDMS / 90.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM-v1/v2 navtest and reaches 38.7 HD-Score on closed-loop HUGSIM in a zero-shot setting, demonstrating leading planning performance across both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations. Extensive experiments further demonstrate that planning-shaped future representations provide an effective and deployable form of foresight for world-action models.

papers.title_en: BridgeGuard: Explicit Safety Drift for Diffusion-based Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Zhenjun Qiu, Jianing Huang, Dongang Liu, Baiyu Du, Yixun Niu, Hao Yang, Xinyu Huang, Chuan Hu, Shu Liu
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶的安全约束扩散规划,结合学习到的距离场
papers.tldr: 扩散式驾驶规划器能生成多样轨迹，但在分布偏移下易输出不安全轨迹。BridgeGuard 在去噪中逐步增强约束项，将中间轨迹推向场景相关安全域，并在低维曲线空间修正；DistanceFieldNet 预测时变距离场。Bench2Drive 上，BridgeDrive 驾驶分/成功率由 87.99/74.99% 升至 90.88/76.36%，DiffusionDrive^geo 由 80.79/58.18% 升至 90.46/74.09%。感知与规划器冻结，实现即插即用与跨模型泛化，并给出理想连续桥的终端安全条件。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion-based driving planners capture diverse behaviors but can generate unsafe trajectories under distribution shift. We propose BridgeGuard, a safety-constrained diffusion planning method that progressively strengthens a constraint term during denoising to drive intermediate trajectories toward a scene-dependent safety domain. Corrections operate in a low-dimensional curve space, promoting geometric coherence. A learned module, DistanceFieldNet, predicts a time-dependent distance field from bird's-eye-view features. Value and spatial-gradient supervision at queries sampled beyond expert trajectories teaches this field about both safe and unsafe regions. The learned field supplies the constraint term through safety injection while the pretrained perception backbone and planner remain frozen. We further establish sufficient conditions for terminal safety in an idealized continuous-time bridge. On Bench2Drive, BridgeGuard improves driving score/success rate from 87.99/74.99% to 90.88/76.36% for BridgeDrive and from 80.79/58.18% to 90.46/74.09% for $\text{DiffusionDrive}^{\text{geo}}$, demonstrating cross-model generalization.

papers.title_en: SDPAD: A Fully Spike-Driven Pipeline for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Chengjun Zhang, Yuhao Zhang, Jie Yang, Mohamad Sawan
papers.evidence: 全脉冲驱动的端到端自动驾驶流水线，含BEV感知与规划
papers.tldr: 端到端自动驾驶要求规划器兼顾精度与能耗，但ANN规划器计算密集，SNN精度落后。SDPAD提出全脉冲驱动规划流程：量化ANN2SNN转换感知栈，用Spike-3D-Lift将多视图图像提升至BEV空间，再由Spike-QFormer融合自车、智能体与地图查询并回归路点，全程脉冲门控、单次前向推理。在nuScenes开环取得0.40m平均L2误差与0.12%碰撞率，能耗仅69.9mJ；NAVSIM闭环达86.3 PDMS，超越SNN规划器SAD 4.3分并媲美主流ANN规划器。这是首个全脉冲驱动的端到端规划器。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end autonomous driving demands trajectory planners that are both highly accurate and cheap enough for edge deployment. State-of-the-art artificial neural network (ANN) planners meet the accuracy requirement at the cost of heavy dense computation, while spiking neural networks (SNNs)---though promising orders-of-magnitude energy savings through sparse, event-driven arithmetic---still lag far behind in planning accuracy. We present \textbf{SDPAD}, a fully spike-driven end-to-end planning pipeline that closes this gap. SDPAD converts a pre-trained ANN perception stack into integer-spike form via quantized ANN2SNN conversion, lifts multi-view images into the bird's-eye-view (BEV) space with a spike-driven-max (SDM) depth distribution (Spike-3D-Lift), and plans through the Spike-QFormer, a spiking query transformer in which ego, agent, and map queries distilled from the BEV scene are fused by learnable waypoint queries via cross-attention, followed by deformable spike-cross-attention refinement. Every operation is gated by integer spikes and inference is a single feed-forward pass without temporal simulation loops. On the nuScenes open-loop benchmark, SDPAD achieves an average $L_2$ error of 0.40\,m and a collision rate of 0.12\%, on par with strong ANN planners while consuming 69.9\,mJ---less than 2\% of recent ANN baselines. In closed-loop evaluation on the NAVSIM navtest split, SDPAD reaches 86.3 PDMS, surpassing the previous SNN planner SAD by 4.3 points and matching mainstream ANN planners at a fraction of their energy. To our knowledge, SDPAD is the first fully spike-driven planner evaluated in end-to-end autonomous driving, demonstrating that SNNs can rival dense ANNs in complex driving tasks.

papers.title_en: FPD-Drive: Future Policy Distillation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Li-Heng Chen, Qifeng Chen, Chengwei Wu, Yingjie Zhang, Sheng Yang, Hongbo Fu, Shaoqing Ren
papers.evidence: 端到端驾驶规划器,通过未来特权多目标蒸馏提升安全候选选择
papers.tldr: 端到端自动驾驶仅用实际执行轨迹训练，缺乏对多种有效行为的监督，多目标监督又使安全候选选择更难。FPD-Drive提出未来特权多目标蒸馏，将教师借助未来观测得到的高质量轨迹迁移给学生，并用安全感知分数校正优化候选排序。基础模型在NAVSIM v1/v2达94.9 PDMS与55.9 EPDMS，Pro版提升至95.5与58.1，HUGSIM零样本闭环HD-Score 45.1、RC 55.3。该工作兼顾多轨迹监督与安全选择，部署无需未来观测或教师推理。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end autonomous driving models are typically trained on real-world driving logs, which record only the trajectory actually executed in each scene. This provides limited supervision for learning alternative valid behaviors. Multi-target supervision can mitigate this limitation, but broader trajectory coverage makes safe candidate selection more challenging. We propose FPD-Drive, an end-to-end planner that distills privileged future knowledge into a visual driving policy to improve both multi-trajectory supervision and safety selection. Specifically, we introduce Future-Privileged Multi-Target Distillation to transfer diverse, high-quality trajectory targets from a teacher with access to recorded future observations to the student. These targets extend supervision beyond the single recorded human trajectory. For candidate selection, we further introduce Safety-Aware Score Correction to correct ranking errors between nearby safe and unsafe candidates and raise underestimated safety scores of safe candidates. At deployment, the student requires neither future observations nor teacher inference. Our base model achieves 94.9 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest and 55.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navhard. The scaled FPD-Drive-Pro improves these scores to 95.5 PDMS and 58.1 EPDMS, respectively, achieving SOTA performance among the compared methods on both benchmarks. Zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM further yields an HD-Score of 45.1 and RC of 55.3.

papers.title_en: ManeuverFlow: Maneuver Hypothesis Generation with Future Evidence for Trajectory Evaluation and Refinement in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Yuhao Wei, Yong Chen, Chen Yang, Yingchen Wang, Delin Ouyang, Lingfeng Qi, Qi Lan, Zhanhua Zhang, Jie Li, Guofa Li
papers.evidence: 端到端自动驾驶的轨迹生成、评估与精炼
papers.tldr: 复杂场景端到端规划需覆盖多样驾驶意图，并依据场景上下文与未来风险选择合适轨迹，但多查询回归易坍缩为单一模式，锚点或生成式规划器也受候选集规模限制：小候选集覆盖不足，大候选集生成与打分开销高。ManeuverFlow 一步生成不同意图轨迹，并利用当前与未来证据进行评分和精炼。在 NAVSIM v1/v2 navtest 上取得 90.6 PDMS 与 90.1 EPDMS，在 WorldEngine 3DGS 闭环基准上获最高 PDMS* 75.19/74.58。为复杂场景轨迹选择提供高效方案，实现候选覆盖与效率的平衡。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end planning in complex scenes must model diverse driving intentions and select the most appropriate trajectory using scene context and future risks. However, multi-query regression may collapse to one mode, while anchor-based and generative planners share a scaling bottleneck: small candidate sets limit maneuver coverage or discovery of high-quality trajectories, whereas large sets increase generation and scoring costs. We propose ManeuverFlow to generate trajectories for distinct intentions in one step and evaluate and refine them using current and future evidence. The model selects relevant maneuver modes, draws corresponding noise from the Gaussian mixture prior, and maps it to intention-specific trajectories through a maneuver-routed mixture-of-experts MeanFlow field. Current features and future features predicted by the world model are aggregated along each candidate path into trajectory-specific evidence for PDM-factor prediction. Using the same evidence, the refiner predicts local Frenet residuals for selected candidates; refined and retained candidates are then jointly re-scored for selection. With a lightweight TransFuser-style ResNet-34 backbone, ManeuverFlow achieves 90.6 PDMS and 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v1/v2 navtest, respectively. On WorldEngine's recent 3DGS closed-loop benchmark, it attains the highest listed PDMS$^\ast$ scores of 75.19 and 74.58 under logged and IDM-controlled traffic, respectively. Code: https://github.com/wyh-autonomy/maneuverflow.

papers.title_en: Reflect-VLA: Internalizing Reflective Guidance via Dual-Path On-Policy Self-Distillation for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Yuechen Luo, He Chong, Fang Li, Shaoqing Xu, Hexin Zhang, Ruiqi Zhang, Ziying Song, Lei Yang, Zhi-Xin Yang, Fuxi Wen
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶VLA规划的反思引导强化学习
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶VLA模型的强化学习依赖标量轨迹奖励，难以定位场景理解、行为选择与轨迹执行中的具体错误，长尾场景纠错信号不足。Reflect-VLA将反思引导作为训练期特权信息，通过双路径同策略自蒸馏Dual-OPSD，对学生高风险轨迹蒸馏密集纠正分布，对可靠轨迹自模仿。在NAVSIM v1/v2与Bench2Drive上，单次前向推理即获有竞争力规划性能，训练时间较RL降低90%以上。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement Learning (RL) substantially improves planning performance in autonomous-driving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. However, existing RL methods rely on scalar trajectory rewards that measure overall quality but fail to identify specific planning errors or provide actionable correction signals. In long-tail scenarios, errors in scene understanding, behavior selection, and trajectory execution are compressed into a single score. We observe that Reflective Guidance turns trajectory evaluation into explicit diagnoses and corrective instructions, substantially improving planning accuracy. Yet such guidance requires an initial prediction and its evaluation results, making it unavailable for direct single-pass inference. We propose Reflect-VLA, which treats Reflective Guidance as training-time privileged information and internalizes its planning benefits through Dual-Path On-Policy Self-Distillation (Dual-OPSD). Unlike scalar-reward optimization, Dual-OPSD uses the driving score only to route student-generated trajectories. It distills dense token-level corrective distributions from the teacher for risky trajectories while applying self-imitation to preserve reliable ones. To provide reliable corrective distributions on student rollouts, the teacher is progressively constructed through Driving-Knowledge Pretraining, Planning-and-Refinement SFT, and Self-Refinement Rejection Sampling. At inference time, Reflect-VLA generates trajectories in a single pass without explicit guidance or iterative refinement. Experiments on NAVSIM v1/v2 and Bench2Drive demonstrate competitive planning performance while reducing training time by over 90% compared with RL.

papers.title_en: SimVTA: Simulation-Grounded Video-Trajectory Alignment for Driving World Action Models
papers.authors: Changhui Jing, Haochen Tian, Hongchen Li, Tianyu Li, Caojun Wang, Zihao Zhang, Yanhao Liu, Chengen Xie, Bailin Li, Hao Zhao, Zhenjie Yang
papers.evidence: 驾驶世界动作模型与仿真驱动的视频轨迹对齐
papers.tldr: 驾驶世界动作模型的后训练面临轨迹替代方案缺乏未来视频监督的问题：日志只记录实际轨迹的视频。SimVTA 提出仿真接地的视频-轨迹对齐框架，先采样候选轨迹，并用3DGS重建场景与真实世界仿真器渲染高奖励候选的未来视频。再以GRPO优化规划，并用流匹配损失对齐渲染视频与轨迹，从而更新共享表征。在NAVSIM v1上PDMS从86.2提升至91.3，v2达88.2 EPDMS，HUGSIM闭环平均HD-Score为38.8，验证了视频监督对规划的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Driving world action models (WAMs) learn from paired trajectories and future observations. Post-training with reinforcement learning allows the policy to explore alternative trajectories and improve planning using driving rewards. However, driving logs contain future videos only for the recorded trajectories, leaving these alternatives without corresponding visual supervision. Thus, we introduce SimVTA, a simulation-grounded post-training framework that combines trajectory optimization with video supervision. First, we sample candidate trajectories for each observation and use a real-world simulator (e.g., World Engine) to render future videos for high-reward candidates in real-world scenes reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). This provides trajectory-matched supervision independent of the model's own predictions. Under a limited rendering budget, we prioritize video supervision for higher-error futures among these rendered candidates. Finally, we optimize trajectory planning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and use a flow-matching loss on the matched videos to update shared representations. At inference time, the model predicts trajectories directly, without simulator calls. On NAVSIM v1, applying SimVTA to a WAM initialization improves PDMS from 86.2 to 91.3 (+5.1). It achieves 88.2 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and an average HD-Score of 38.8 in closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM. Ablations show that updating shared representations with video supervision improves planning, while prioritizing higher-error futures among high-reward trajectories further improves performance.

papers.title_en: YOUDrive: Driving Style as a Composable Direction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Guantian Zheng, Lidong Yu, Tianyu Gao, Jiaxing Chen, Jiashu Li, Chen Lv
papers.evidence: 面向端到端驾驶的可组合风格控制视觉-语言-动作规划器
papers.tldr: 端到端自动驾驶策略虽任务表现强，却缺乏对加速、刹车和跟车距离等驾驶风格的连续控制。YOUDrive是一种视觉-语言-动作规划器，将每位教师行为蒸馏为任务向量，在规划器表征中形成可缩放、可组合的风格方向，无需重训主干即可在推理时调节。结合流匹配解码器生成多模态且运动学可行的轨迹。在NAVSIM navtest上，单一系数可单调控制六种教师人格的激进程度，PDMS保持0.90以上并达0.954。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end driving policies can achieve strong task performance while offering limited control over their driving style. Driving style describes how a vehicle accelerates, brakes, and maintains distance. Policies trained without explicit preference conditioning lack a direct mechanism for adjusting these behaviors at inference. We propose YOUDrive, a vision--language--action planner for continuous and composable driving-style control. Each teacher's behavior is distilled into a task vector, a learned parameter update that induces a style direction in the planner's representation. These directions can be scaled and combined at inference without retraining the backbone. Conditioned on these directions, a flow-matching decoder models a multimodal trajectory distribution and generates kinematically feasible motion alternatives. We introduce the Style Alignment Score (SAS) to describe human-referenced kinematic behavior after safety and task gating. On NAVSIM navtest, a single coefficient monotonically controls assertiveness across six teacher-derived personas, while PDMS remains above 0.90 across the tested individual and blended configurations, reaching 0.954. Further analyses reveal systematic policy-specific kinematics after controlling for scene context, whereas the evaluated discrete style labels provide limited additional explanatory power. Code, checkpoints, and the metric will be released.

papers.title_en: MORE: Learning Motion-Oriented Registers for Driving World Models and Planning
papers.authors: Yingdong Gu, Haoyu Wang, Shaocheng Yan, Zhenjun Zhao, Hao Han, Pengcheng Shi, Xianfei Li, Qinghua Tan, Wenlong Liao, Tao He, Jiayuan Li, Pai Peng
papers.evidence: 面向运动寄存器的驾驶世界模型与规划
papers.tldr: 潜在世界模型可自监督预测未来，但常沿用预训练视觉编码器的稠密特征，导致与运动条件建模和规划不匹配。MORE在视频预训练中学习运动导向寄存器，将自车运动注入少量寄存器，并以其为唯一上下文做掩码块预测，形成紧凑状态瓶颈。在NAVSIM-v2上，EPDMS比最优方法高1.6，推理延迟仅为DriveLaW的1/10。该工作表明可直接在视频预训练阶段学习面向世界建模与规划的状态接口。
papers.abstract_en: By predicting future states, latent world models provide rich self-supervision for end-to-end driving, but often inherit dense features from pretrained visual encoders as their world-state interface. This creates a mismatch: visual pretraining produces information-rich, spatially dense features, but their adaptation for motion-conditioned world modeling and planning is deferred to downstream training. The dense grid also makes future prediction more computationally expensive as visual resolution increases. We therefore argue that video pretraining should directly learn state representations suited to downstream world modeling and planning, rather than relying on downstream training to adapt inherited visual features. We propose ***MORE***, a V-JEPA framework that learns **M**otion-**O**riented **RE**gisters during video pretraining as a shared state interface for driving world models and planning. MORE injects temporally aligned ego motion into a small set of registers and uses them as the sole context for masked patch prediction, channeling dense patch-level supervision through a compact state bottleneck. A complementary blockwise register-masking objective further shapes predictive structure in the register space. During downstream training, the same register space defines the future states predicted by the world model and provides shared scene memory for trajectory generation and scoring. On NAVSIM-v2, MORE outperforms the state of the art by 1.6 in EPDMS, while achieving superior efficiency with only 1/10 the inference latency of DriveLaW. These results support learning the state interface for world modeling and planning directly during video pretraining.

papers.title_en: RM-WAM: Reliable Memory-Augmented World Action Models for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Cui Miao, Junhao Yu, Ping Liu, Ning Yang, Xuhua Chen, He Zheng, Xiaodong Wang, Tao Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向长时程机器人操作的记忆增强世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 长程机器人操作中，现有世界动作模型多依赖当前观测，难以区分视觉相似但历史与阶段不同的状态；直接引入历史又可能带来陈旧、阶段错配和误差污染。RM-WAM将记忆视为依赖上下文的预测资源，用短期视觉状态记忆与潜在事件记忆表示历史，并通过反事实记忆学习估计其效用。基于效用感知门控自适应注入记忆，实验表明该选择性记忆机制能提升长程任务可靠性。
papers.abstract_en: World Action Models (WAMs) improve robotic manipulation by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, yet most existing methods make decisions primarily from the current observation. This limits their reliability in long-horizon tasks, where visually similar states may correspond to different interaction histories and task stages. Moreover, directly incorporating historical observations can introduce stale, stage-mismatched, or error-contaminated information, leading to inaccurate world prediction and accumulated closed-loop errors. We propose RM-WAM, a reliable memory-augmented World Action Model that treats memory as a context-dependent predictive resource rather than universally useful historical context. RM-WAM represents history using complementary short-term visual state memory and latent event memory, which respectively capture recent interaction dynamics and longer-term state transitions. A counterfactual memory learning scheme varies the accessible history while keeping the current inputs and prediction targets fixed, enabling the model to learn a context-dependent utility estimate for historical memory. Based on this estimate, a utility-aware gating mechanism adaptively controls memory injection into the world-action backbone. Experiments demonstrate that RM-WAM highlights the importance of reliable and selective memory utilization in long-horizon tasks.

papers.title_en: $Δ$ Flow Matching for Robot Foundation Models
papers.authors: Kuangji Zuo, Tuo An, Xinying Guo, Gen Li, Mengfei Zhao, Jiaqi Bai, Bofan Lyu, Zhuoyuan Yu, Jinghan Yang, Jiayi Li, Jindou Jia, Jianfei Yang
papers.evidence: 面向机器人基础模型与世界动作模型的高效流匹配
papers.tldr: 机器人基础模型的流匹配通常从固定高斯先验生成动作或未来视觉状态，忽略过去与未来之间的时序连续性，导致训练昂贵且需迭代采样。Δ-flow 用近期历史加轻噪声构造源分布，使源更接近目标，只需学习小残差 Δ，并实现高效单步推理。将其集成到 π0.5、ImageWAM 与 Fast-WAM 后，ImageWAM 一个 epoch 达 90%，Fast-WAM 两个 epoch 达 95%，单步推理加速 1.54–4.45 倍，动作 jerk 降 4.5 倍。该方法在 LIBERO-Plus 上达 SOTA，并可免重训练迁移到预训练 WAM，显著提升效率、泛化与跨任务表现。
papers.abstract_en: Flow matching is a common generative recipe for robot foundation models. Vision-language-action models (VLAs) generate action chunks, while world-action models (WAMs) additionally generate future visual states. Both start generation from a fixed Gaussian prior, despite temporal continuity between past and future states and actions. This requires costly training and iterative sampling, especially for WAMs with an additional visual branch. We introduce $Δ$-flow, which constructs the source from recent history with mild noise rather than from a fixed Gaussian prior. This moves the source closer to the target, reducing transport to a small residual $Δ$ that can be learned efficiently and enables single-step inference. We integrate $Δ$-flow into the VLA policy $π_{0.5}$ and the WAM policies ImageWAM and Fast-WAM. On LIBERO, ImageWAM reaches 90% success in one epoch rather than six, and Fast-WAM reaches 95% in two epochs rather than eight. With LoRA fine-tuning, $π_{0.5}$ exceeds its baseline's five-epoch performance after one epoch. Single-step inference gives $1.54\times$, $2.49\times$, and $4.45\times$ speedups on $π_{0.5}$, ImageWAM, and Fast-WAM, respectively. It preserves action smoothness, achieving a $4.5\times$ reduction in action jerk compared with one-step Gaussian sampling. $Δ$-flow reaches state-of-the-art generalization performance on LIBERO-Plus. Action-history sources can be applied to pretrained WAM policies without retraining. Replacing the Gaussian action source at inference largely preserves task success with a single sampling step and can slightly improve it. We further study how action representation and visual information in action learning affect history-to-future prediction in $Δ$-flow. These results show that $Δ$-flow is simple yet effective, improving the efficiency and generalization of robot foundation models.

papers.title_en: Directional Pullback Regularization for Long-Horizon Rollout of Latent World Models in Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Shatadal Mishra, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Nejib Ammar
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶的潜在世界模型长时程推演与运动学正则
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶潜世界模型常在无约束潜空间做长时程推演，忽略地面车辆非完整约束。作者提出方向性回拉正则化 DPR：在解码状态空间构造运动学感知的各向异性黎曼度量，经解码器雅可比回拉至潜空间，使横向运动潜方向代价更高。在10秒开环自车运动推演中，DPR在1/3/5/10步训练设定下均优于ULR和EPR，3步训练相对ULR降低约44%最终位移误差。方法不改编码器-动力学-解码器主干，为长时程潜推演提供运动感知几何正则化。
papers.abstract_en: Learned world models for autonomous driving operate in unconstrained latent spaces, yet the physical systems they represent are governed by strict non-holonomic constraints: ground vehicles cannot realize instantaneous pure lateral motion. We study long-horizon latent rollout modeling for autonomous driving and ask whether rollout quality can be improved by assigning a motion-aware geometry to latent transitions, rather than by redesigning the predictor architecture. Starting from an unconstrained latent rollout baseline, we introduce Directional Pullback Regularization (DPR), a training time method that defines a kinematics-aware anisotropic Riemannian metric in decoded state space and pulls it back through the decoder Jacobian to the latent manifold. The resulting latent-space metric assigns higher cost to latent directions that decode to lateral vehicle motion, while preserving the original encoder-dynamics-decoder backbone. This yields a clean three-way comparison among an Unconstrained Latent Rollout model (ULR), an Euclidean Pullback Regularization ablation (EPR), and the full directional method (DPR). We evaluate all models on open-loop ego-motion rollout over a common 10-second test horizon, using training rollout lengths of 1, 3, 5, and 10 steps. Across all four training regimes, DPR achieves lower 10-second final displacement error than both ULR and EPR. The strongest relative accuracy gain appears for models trained with 3-step rollout supervision, where DPR reduces the 10-second final displacement error by approximately 44 percent relative to ULR. The strongest overall control-relevant tradeoff is obtained for longer rollout-trained models, especially at 10 steps, where DPR simultaneously improves displacement error, lateral motion consistency, and forward motion preservation relative to both ULR and EPR.

papers.title_en: Language2Drive: Do Vision-Language-Action Models Really Follow the Instructions in Autonomous Driving?
papers.authors: Zihan You, Zehua Fan, Wenqi Lyu, Aoqi Wang, Ni Wang, Yifei Yang, Linge Zhao, Huan Li, Sining Ang, Yuguang Yang, Jueyu Chen, Xiangyu Li, Qianshan Wei, Jieyuan Pei, Yuxin Wang, Zhiwen Chen, Jiaqi Li, Wenxuan Song, Yanyuan Qiao, Benjin Zhu, Haoang Li, Yan Wang
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶的视觉语言动作模型指令遵循评测
papers.tldr: 问题背景：现有VLA驾驶模型用自然语言指令控制行为，但闭环基准只测路线完成、安全、规则，未验证语言是否真正决定可行行为。核心方法：提出Language2Drive基准及配对反事实单元PCU，固定初始场景仅改指令，覆盖四类指令跟随范围，并在CARLA闭环、真实重建场景和开环基准中评测。关键结果：93.2%成功rollout在替代可行指令下无成功配对，主要表现为单侧完成。贡献意义：揭示孤立成功和驾驶分数会高估语言跟随能力，当前VLA在匹配反事实测试下缺乏可靠指令跟随。
papers.abstract_en: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models increasingly use natural-language instructions to condition autonomous driving behavior. Yet existing closed-loop benchmarks primarily measure route completion, safety, and rule compliance, leaving a fundamental question unresolved: does language actually determine which feasible behavior the vehicle executes? A trajectory may be safe and successful while still violating or even ignoring the passenger's instruction. To address this, we introduce \ltd, a benchmark designed to directly test this capability. Its key evaluation unit, the paired counterfactual unit (PCU), holds the initial driving scene fixed while changing only the instruction. This design enables us to distinguish isolated instruction success from counterfactual paired success across four instruction-following scopes. To test whether this distinction persists across evaluation regimes, we instantiate Language2Drive in complementary closed-loop CARLA simulation, reconstructed real-world scenes, and open-loop driving benchmarks, including our released CARLA-Language2Drive simulator with purpose-built maps. Evaluating representative driving VLAs across these settings reveals a striking mismatch between strong driving competence and weak language control: 93.2% of successful rollouts do not have a successful counterpart under the alternative feasible instruction. This failure is dominated by one-sided completion, where a model repeatedly executes one preferred behavior but fails when the same scene requires the counterfactual alternative. These results expose two fundamental limitations of current evaluation: isolated success and driving scores, which are widely used by conventional driving benchmarks, can substantially overstate language-following capability, while current driving VLAs themselves lack reliable instruction following under matched counterfactual tests.

papers.title_en: AUGUstus: Autonomous Driving VLA Model with Unified Generation and Understanding
papers.authors: Yuqi Ye, Caigao Jiang, Zhuonan Wang, Congyuan Pei, Chao Qu, Changhao Peng, Junhong Lin, Qize Yu, Zetian Song, Guangzhao Fu, Chongruo Wu, Shiyu Huang, Shuchang Zhou, Honggou Yang, Wei Gao
papers.evidence: 统一生成与理解、面向自动驾驶规划的VLA模型
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶VLA模型面临两难：回归或流式方法为低延迟直接生成动作，却退化为视觉-动作模型，未充分利用VLM理解，导致动作不安全且难解释；自回归方法逐步生成思维链与动作，理解充分但延迟过高。AUGUstus将扩散式动作生成与自回归思维链理解统一在一个模型中，让理解仅服务于生成。其AUGUstus-mode先输出动作再输出思维链，训练时由思维链监督可靠动作，推理仅需动作，实现低延迟。AUGUstus-GRPO统一优化动作与思维链。实验在NAVSIMv1/v2与nuScenes取得SOTA，并初步实车部署达12Hz。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models show strong potential for end-to-end autonomous driving by leveraging world knowledge and understanding to excel in long-tail scenarios. However, current VLAs have two limitations: 1) Degeneration into vision-action (VA) models. For low latency, regression/flow-based methods directly generate actions but underuse VLM understanding, causing unsafe, unexplainable actions. 2) Autoregressive high latency. Autoregressive methods sequentially generate chain-of-thought (CoT) and action tokens, fully leveraging VLM understanding, but high latency hinders deployment. To enable low-latency deployment while using CoT to assist action generation, we propose AUGUstus, an Autonomous-driving VLA model with Unified Generation and Understanding. We unify diffusion-based action generation and autoregressive CoT understanding in one model, where understanding only serves generation. Joint CoT supervision preserves VLM spatial understanding in shared representation for safer, more accurate trajectories. AUGUstus-mode orders action generation before CoT, so CoT supervises reliable actions during training while inference needs only action output, enabling low latency. AUGUstus-GRPO, a unified GRPO algorithm, jointly optimizes action and CoT, improving action performance. Experiments show AUGUstus achieves 94.6 PDMS on NAVSIMv1 and 90.7 EPDMS on NAVSIMv2, SOTA planning without scorer module. On nuScenes, it achieves average L2 error 0.27 m and average collision rate 0.05%, best among compared methods. To validate AUGUstus practicality, we train on in-house data with 512 NVIDIA H800 GPUs for ~2 days, evaluate on an internal 1,000 km dataset, and preliminarily deploy on a real vehicle, achieving 12 Hz operation. Project page: https://augustus-ad.github.io

papers.title_en: OccWAM: Occupancy World-Action Models with Joint Scene-to-Ego Flow Matching
papers.authors: Qihang Huang, Wenhui Huang, Collister Chua, Shiyu Fang, Zhan Chen, Songyan Zhang, Zhidong Wang, Daiying Tian, Chen Lv
papers.evidence: 面向端到端自动驾驶的占据世界-动作模型
papers.tldr: 现有占用感知规划器多采用层级耦合或并行多任务方式，占用预测与动作生成之间存在显式生成顺序或角色不对称，限制了世界预测与动作生成在轨迹形成中的双向交互。OccWAM 提出占用原生世界-动作模型，以场景表示为条件，通过流匹配联合生成稠密未来占用与连续自车轨迹，并引入场景到自车的两阶段世界-动作流匹配：先预测场景中心占用与绝对轨迹，再将同一预测世界重索引到自车未来坐标系，用相邻位姿增量与第二次联合流细化自车中心占用与运动。在 Bench2Drive 与 nuScenes 上，闭环驾驶、开环规划与未来占用预测均取得最优性能。
papers.abstract_en: Occupancy world models provide a structured, metric representation of future driving scenes, making them a promising basis for end-to-end autonomous driving. However, existing occupancy-aware planners typically couple occupancy prediction and action generation through either hierarchical coupling or parallel multi-task learning. Hierarchical methods use occupancy either as a fully predicted future preceding action generation or as an action-conditioned rollout for trajectory evaluation, whereas parallel multi-task methods predict occupancy alongside planning through a separate branch or auxiliary objective. These interfaces retain either an explicit generation order or a role asymmetry, limiting reciprocal interaction between world prediction and action generation during trajectory formation. We propose OccWAM, an occupancy-native world-action model that jointly generates dense future occupancy and continuous ego trajectories via flow matching conditioned on scene representations. Building on this joint formulation, we introduce scene-to-ego world-action flow matching, a two-stage formulation. The first stage predicts scene-centric occupancy together with an absolute ego trajectory, providing a stable representation of future scene evolution. The same predicted world is then re-indexed into the future ego frames induced by the initial trajectory, where ego motion is represented through adjacent pose increments and a second joint flow refines ego-centric occupancy and motion for action-aligned planning. Unlike video-based world-action models, OccWAM preserves explicit semantic geometry for direct planning reasoning without pixel synthesis. Extensive experiments on Bench2Drive and nuScenes demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in closed-loop driving, open-loop planning, and future occupancy prediction.

papers.title_en: Beyond Safe Execution: Safe Online Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving with Value Calibration and Adaptive Guidance
papers.authors: Zeqiao Li, Yijing Wang, Haoyu Wang, Zheng Li, Zhiqiang Zuo
papers.evidence: 面向驾驶策略的安全在线强化学习微调,结合CBF-MPC安全过滤
papers.tldr: 在线强化学习可让自动驾驶策略适应部署变化，但训练全程安全探索仍是难题，仅靠安全过滤无法保证稳定改进。SOAR-Flow面向离线初始化的Flow策略进行安全在线微调，用CBF-MPC过滤危险动作，并引入高斯回报感知价值校准、配对纠正学习与干预预测器。仿真和UGV实验表明，该方法提升驾驶性能并减少对安全纠正的依赖。其贡献在于兼顾硬执行约束与持续任务改进。
papers.abstract_en: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables driving policies to adapt to changing deployment conditions, but requires safe exploration throughout training. Safety filtering alone does not ensure stable policy improvement or reduced dependence on corrections. We propose Safe Online Adaptive Refinement (SOAR-Flow), a framework for safe and stable online fine-tuning of offline-initialized Flow-based driving policies. A control barrier function (CBF)--model predictive control (MPC) filter corrects potentially unsafe actions before execution. To support stable policy updates, we introduce Gaussian-return-aware value calibration based on calibrated Q-learning (Cal-QL), using recorded behavior returns and predicted return variability to smooth conservative critic updates and mitigate policy degradation. Paired corrective learning teaches feasible action adjustments, while an intervention-to-go predictor encourages decisions requiring fewer future corrections. Its predictions also regulate guidance strength, allowing recovery supervision to weaken as predicted dependence decreases. Together with gradually reduced calibration regularization, this supports continued task improvement while preserving hard execution constraints. We analyze conditions for safe execution at control steps and diminishing auxiliary learning influences. We evaluate SOAR-Flow in simulation and on an uncrewed ground vehicle (UGV). The results demonstrate improved driving performance and reduced reliance on safety corrections during protected online fine-tuning. The demonstration video and project overview are available at https://lzqw.github.io/SOAR-Flow/.

papers.title_en: DriveWLA: Unifying Future Dynamics and Scene Semantics through World-Language-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Shuzheng Wang, Haoxuan Li, Shengzhen Li, Chenxi Wu, Yajing Sun, Lu Hou, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang
papers.evidence: 统一世界—语言—动作模型，预测未来动态并生成轨迹
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶中VLM语义理解与世界模型未来演化各有优势，但整合二者生成轨迹仍具挑战。DriveWLA提出基于MoT的统一World-Language-Action模型，含世界、语言、动作三专家，并用Cross-Expert Attention对齐语义与动态表示。进一步用Flow-GRPO强化学习后训练优化动作专家。在NAVSIM v1/v2取得92.3 PDMS与90.1 EPDMS，并零样本泛化到HUGSIM、nuScenes、Bench2Drive，验证统一建模有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and world models have demonstrated strong capabilities in semantic understanding and future scene evolution for autonomous driving. However, effectively integrating both capabilities for trajectory generation remains challenging. In this work, we propose DriveWLA, a unified World-Language-Action model based on Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) that jointly models semantic understanding, future scene dynamics, and trajectory generation. DriveWLA consists of three experts: a World Expert for future prediction, a Language Expert for semantic understanding, and an Action Expert for trajectory generation. We further introduce Cross-Expert Attention, which enables controlled information flow across experts while aligning semantic and dynamic representations. To improve trajectory generation beyond imitation learning, we apply Flow-GRPO reinforcement learning post-training to refine the Action Expert. Extensive experiments show that DriveWLA achieves superior performance in both open-loop and closed-loop evaluation. DriveWLA achieves 92.3 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, demonstrating strong performance among VLM-based and world-model-based planners. Without specific fine-tuning, DriveWLA further demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization to HUGSIM, nuScenes, and Bench2Drive. These results validate the effectiveness of our unified World-Language-Action modeling, establishing DriveWLA as a generalizable framework for autonomous driving.

papers.title_en: WoVR+: World Model as Reliable Simulator for Versatile VLA Policy Optimization with RL
papers.authors: Shangqing Zhou, Zhennan Jiang, Ning Ma, Xin Fu, Yupeng Zheng, Shuai Tian, Huangrui Li, Jiahao Liu, Chao Yu, Zhongpu Xia, Haoran Li, Dongbin Zhao
papers.evidence: 以世界模型作为可靠仿真器优化VLA策略的强化学习框架
papers.tldr: 针对VLA强化学习中真实交互昂贵、动作条件世界模型易产生幻觉误导策略优化的问题，WoVR+重构学习环境与想象交互协议：对齐VLA接口的世界模型提供多视角预测与本体感知更新，块级噪声平衡探索与预测稳定。长时任务采用阶段局部想象训练、阶段入口重置与可控采样。RoboTwin和6个真机任务成功率较SFT提升21.09%和16.7%，长时手机包装从30%升至75%。
papers.abstract_en: Action-conditioned world models can reduce costly real-robot interaction in reinforcement learning for Vision-Language-Action models (VLA-RL), but hallucinations can mislead policy optimization. Extending them to richer VLA interfaces and long-horizon tasks raises challenges in spatiotemporal and cross-modal consistency, exploration-reliability balance in RL, and compounding rollout errors. We present WoVR+, extending WoVR's hallucination-aware WM-RL framework by redesigning the learned environment and imagined interaction protocol: A VLA-interface-aligned world model provides multi-view prediction and proprioceptive updates while mitigating hallucinations. Chunk-wise noise preserves flow-based policy exploration while limiting prediction-degrading action jitter. For long-horizon tasks, stage-local imagined training combines stage-entry resets, stage-specific rewards, local horizons, and controllable sampling to shorten generated prefixes and balance training across stages. WoVR+ improves success over SFT by 21.09% and 16.7% on RoboTwin and 6 real-robot tasks. Long-horizon phone-packaging success rises from 30% to 75%. Videos are available at https://youmo445.github.io/WoVR_Plus.github.io/.

papers.title_en: Beyond Planning: Differentiable Control-in-the-loop End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Zhidong Wang, Zirui Li, Zitong Shan, Zhiqi Mao, Qihang Huang, Zhan Chen, Jingsong Liang, Han Yu, Chen Lv
papers.evidence: 可微控制闭环的端到端自动驾驶
papers.tldr: 端到端自动驾驶虽能直接从传感器规划轨迹，但规划到控制仍依赖手工跟踪控制器，阻断了车辆运动回传到网络的梯度，并受不可微动力学、专家标签混叠、控制与重规划频率失配及模型差异困扰。DIVA将辨识的执行器级车辆模型嵌入训练闭环，形成从感知到车辆状态的可微链路，并用学习型控制解码器基于滚动状态监督，绕开混叠控制标签；速率一致参数化实现异步执行。在Bench2Drive闭环基准上驾驶得分86.7，超SOTA 3.3分，平均加加速度近半，刹车切换减少64%，显著模型失配下仍保持路径跟踪精度。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved remarkable progress by planning trajectories directly from raw sensor data. Yet the step from planning to control still relies on hand-tuned tracking controllers that block the gradient path from vehicle motion back to the network. This gap stems from non-differentiable vehicle dynamics, aliased supervision from coarsely sampled expert labels, rate mismatch between high-rate control and low-rate re-planning, and vehicle model discrepancies between training and deployment. This paper proposes DIVA (Differentiable Identified Vehicle dynamics for end-to-end Autonomous driving) to close this gap. An identified actuator-level vehicle model is embedded in the training loop of the end-to-end driving network, forming a differentiable chain from perception to vehicle states. A learning-based control decoder replaces the external controller and is supervised on the rolled-out vehicle states, bypassing the aliased control-input labels. A rate-consistent control-input parameterization reconciles the heterogeneous sampling rates and enables asynchronous execution with a 3.8 ms control-only cycle. On-policy re-identification and an online disturbance observer address training-time distribution shift and deployment-time model mismatch respectively. On the closed-loop Bench2Drive benchmark, DIVA achieves a driving score of 86.7, surpassing the widely adopted state-of-the-art approach by 3.3 points while nearly halving mean jerk and reducing brake switching by 64%, and maintains superior path tracking accuracy under significant vehicle model mismatch at deployment.

papers.title_en: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
papers.authors: Ao Liang, Youquan Liu, Mingxiao Li, Wei Chow, Lingdong Kong, Yue Liao, Dongyue Lu, Yu Yang, Wei Yin, Runnan Chen
papers.evidence: 从视觉运动推导驾驶动作的世界-动作模型
papers.tldr: 世界动作模型常将动作专家训练在独立于视觉动态的轨迹表示上，限制视觉运动向驾驶决策转化。VITAL提出视觉诱导动作标记器，将视觉运动骨架与紧凑残差结合，以流匹配联合预测两者，无需推理时生成未来图像。单步去噪在NAVSIM v1 navtest达90.8 PDMS，接近十步且端到端推理提速3.29倍；无需重训在v2 navtest达91.1 EPDMS，navhard达38.6。该工作让视觉运动成为主预测目标，并支持残差坐标上的有界强化后训练。
papers.abstract_en: World-action models aim to turn visual anticipation into driving decisions, yet typically train action experts on trajectory representations defined independently of visual dynamics. This motivates deriving action targets directly from visual motion. We first examine a simpler setting in which trajectories are reconstructed from recorded future images. Even without the need for future prediction, reconstruction captures the dominant maneuver but leaves centimeter-scale errors. We therefore introduce VITAL (Vision-Induced Tokens for Action Learning), an action tokenizer that couples a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual encoding the trajectory error left by that scaffold. This representation makes visual motion the principal prediction target and gives small metric corrections a separate, normalized learning scale. Using flow matching, the action expert jointly predicts both components from the current image, ego state, and navigation command, without generating future images at inference. The same residual coordinates support bounded reinforcement post-training that refines execution while keeping the predicted visual scaffold fixed. With only one action denoising step, VITAL achieves 90.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, within 0.13 points of its ten-step score at 3.29x the end-to-end inference speed. Without retraining, it achieves 91.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest and 38.6 on navhard. Project page: https://worldbench.github.io/vital

papers.title_en: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Shaoyuan Xie, Zihan Zhang, Jingxuan Wang, Jiashu Qu, Xiaoqing Liang, Lingdong Kong, Junchi Lu, Henrik I. Christensen, Qi Alfred Chen
papers.evidence: 面向冲突感知端到端驾驶的导航条件VLA与世界模型
papers.tldr: VLA模型把自动驾驶的导航接口从固定指令扩展为自由语言，却因此暴露新风险：驾驶员可能下达与场景冲突的不安全指令，甚至被恶意利用，而现有模型在冲突信号下性能骤降。SafeDriveVLA首次显式预测三级导航遵从模式，将冲突推理与动作生成解耦，并利用导航条件世界模型dreaming模拟严格跟随导航的后果来判断其是否安全。在Bench2Drive上取得88.16 DS与68.64% SR，闭环语言跟随提升49.3%，不安全指令下碰撞由60降至38。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions. However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. We present the first benchmark suite that evaluates navigation following and conflict awareness together, along with adversarial robustness. Existing VLAs fall short on both: SimLingo completes no language-instructed lane change in closed loop, and all models degrade sharply under conflicting signals. We propose SafeDriveVLA, the first driving VLA that (1) explicitly predicts a three-level navigation-compliance mode to decouple conflict reasoning from action generation, and (2) uses navigation-conditioned world model dreaming to inform this prediction. Unlike prior world models that roll out expert or planned actions, ours dreams of strictly following the navigation signal, showing when following is safe. SafeDriveVLA reaches 88.16 Driving Score (DS) and 68.64% Success Rate (SR) on Bench2Drive, lifts closed-loop language following by 49.3% and reduces collisions under unsafe instructions from 60 to 38 compared to the best SimLingo variant. Video demonstrations are available on our project page.

papers.title_en: WayFinder: Hierarchical Visual-Language-Action for Zero-Shot Waypoint Generation and Low-Level Kinematic Control
papers.authors: Timothy K Johnsen, Marco Levorato
papers.evidence: 分层视觉语言动作与运动控制
papers.tldr: 视觉语言动作模型泛化性强，但实际部署中常受执行不可靠与针对特定机器人微调成本高的严重制约。WayFinder提出端到端闭环分层VLA框架，将高层任务推理与底层运动控制解耦：离板零样本MLLM生成路点，机载轻量策略异步高频执行运动控制。在AirSim四个复杂环境中测试三种MLLM规模，仅在导航失败时调用高层MLLM，无需微调并减少昂贵推理。结果显示导航成功率最高提升27.45%，优于基线底层策略。
papers.abstract_en: Visual Language Action (VLA) models offer unprecedented generalization for autonomous robots; however, their real-world deployment is frequently bottlenecked by unreliable execution and the prohibitive computational cost of fine-tuning for specific robot embodiments and tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose WayFinder, an end-to-end, closed-loop hierarchical VLA framework that circumvents the need for fine-tuning by decoupling high-level task reasoning from low-level kinematic control. WayFinder utilizes a zero-shot, offboard Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) policy to process linguistic context and state maps for strategic waypoint generation. Asynchronously, a lightweight, onboard policy executes real-time kinematic control at high frequency based on continuous sensor feedback. We evaluate WayFinder in Microsoft AirSim, testing on four environments of varying complexity and three MLLM scales to balance prediction efficacy with computational efficiency. Our results demonstrate that WayFinder achieves superior navigation reliability compared to baseline low-level policies. By querying the high-level MLLM only during navigation failures, WayFinder eliminates the need for fine-tuning, minimizes expensive inferences, and significantly increases navigation success rates by up to 27.45%.

papers.title_en: EVO-WAM: Evolving World Action Models through Video-Action Verification
papers.authors: Shiyang Zhou, Xionghao Wu, Wenbo Li, Shenghe Zheng, Jiyao Zhang, Songsong Yu, Yijun Yang, Jianhui Liu, Haoze Sun, Senqiao Yang, Li Jiang, Jingyong Su, Haoyang Huang, Zhuotao Tian
papers.evidence: 通过自生成视频-动作验证演化世界动作模型以适配机器人任务
papers.tldr: 机器人新任务适应常需额外专家演示，而世界动作模型可自生成视频-动作监督，但视频可能未完成任务且动作不一致。EVO-WAM 用状态预测和锚定多帧上下文实现无外部执行 rollout，并以视觉语言模型筛选任务完成前缀、逆动力学验证视频-动作一致性，迭代训练。RoboTwin 2.0 七个未见任务：Cosmos3 26.9%→68.0%，DreamZero 28.5%→46.4%；真实长时程任务 20.0%→76.7%。
papers.abstract_en: Improving robot policies on new tasks without collecting additional expert demonstrations remains a central challenge in robot learning. World action models (WAMs) use broad video priors to jointly predict future videos and actions, offering a potential source of supervision for adapting to new tasks. However, generated videos may fail to depict task completion, and even visually successful videos may be paired with inconsistent actions that lead to execution failure. We propose EVO-WAM, a framework that adapts WAMs to unseen tasks by learning from their own generated video-action trajectories, without executing candidate actions in an external environment. First, we augment WAM training with state prediction and anchored multi-frame context to enable complete autoregressive rollouts without external execution feedback. Second, we identify reliable training experience by selecting task-completing prefixes with a vision-language model and verifying their video-action consistency with an inverse dynamics model. Third, we iteratively train the WAM on verified prefixes and generate new rollouts with the updated model. On seven unseen RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, EVO-WAM increases average success rates from 26.9% to 68.0% for Cosmos3 and from 28.5% to 46.4% for DreamZero, reaching approximately $2.5\times$ and $1.6\times$ their initial success rates. On three unseen long-horizon composite tasks in the real world, it improves Cosmos3's average success rate from 20.0% to 76.7%, a gain of 56.7 percentage points. Project Page: https://evo-wam.github.io/.

papers.title_en: MotorMind: Scaffolding General Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Bingxuan Li, Siqi Song, Yizhuo Wu, Jiarui Yao, Tong Zhang, Huan Zhang
papers.evidence: 通用视觉语言模型直接驱动机器人完成零样本操作
papers.tldr: 现有视觉-语言-动作模型在新任务与环境中的零样本泛化仍有限，且依赖专用训练，难以直接受益于通用VLM。为此，MotorMind将通用VLM提出的中层动作接入确定性机器人控制与反馈，并辅以异步监控和后台记忆更新，无需任务策略训练、编码智能体或额外接地工具。在LIBERO-PRO上取得66.7%成功率，扰动下53.8%，远超先前零样本方法；真实xArm6上平均95%。这表明合适的中层动作表示与异步执行框架能让通用VLM实现有效零样本操作。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced robotic manipulation, but their zero-shot generalization in new tasks and environments remains limited, and their reliance on specialized training keeps them from benefiting directly from rapidly advancing general-purpose vision-language models (VLMs). In parallel, recent agentic robotic systems leverage VLMs for high-level reasoning or coding agents for robot control, but often depend on extensive external models and tools, introducing additional complexity and cost. This motivates us to ask: Can a general-purpose VLM itself operate a robot more like the human teleoperator by reasoning directly from observations, issuing actions, and continuously adapting to execution feedback, without relying on external models such as learned action experts, coding agents or grounding tools like SAM3? In this work, we introduce MotorMind, a robot manipulation harness that connects VLM-proposed mid-level actions to deterministic robot control and feedback, with asynchronous monitoring and background memory updates. Without task-specific policy training, coding agents, or additional grounding tools such as SAM3, MotorMind achieves 66.7% success on the base LIBERO-PRO suites and 53.8% under perturbations, compared with at most 13.3% and 19.2%, respectively, for the prior zero-shot methods we evaluate. The same interface reaches 95% average success on a real xArm6 robot across direct manipulation and human-perturbation settings. Replacing the backbone with a stronger VLM further improves performance, while the remaining failures - primarily due to visual grounding, embodied reasoning, and action knowledge - decrease as VLM capability improves. These results show that a general-purpose VLM, when equipped with an appropriate mid-level action representation and asynchronous execution harness, can perform effective zero-shot robotic manipulation.

papers.title_en: Rho: A Foundation for Efficiently Adaptable VLA Models
papers.authors: Rho Team, Simran Bagaria, Daphne Chen, Dean Fortier, Jianlong Fu, Michael Harrison, Tess Hellebrekers, Neel Joshi, Andrey Kolobov, Dalton Moore, Galen Mullins, Michael Murray, Eduardo Salinas, Reuben Tan
papers.evidence: 面向双臂操作自适应适配的开源VLA模型
papers.tldr: 通用物理AI需兼具视觉语言理解与跨机器人本体的精确控制，并能高效适配下游任务。作者提出开源权重VLA模型族Rho，面向双臂操作，在YAM Box、UR AI Trainer与FR3 Duo三种本体上系统消融动作专家架构与训练配方。实验表明具身中期训练提升下游适配，Rho变体在仿真与真机任务中匹配或超越现有开源VLA，取得总体最强表现。其内置在线适配模块可凭少量纠正反馈选择观测条件噪声，用约15个纠正回合处理分布边缘任务；作者开源基础模型与本体检查点。
papers.abstract_en: General-purpose physical AI models must combine broad visual and linguistic capabilities with precise control across robot embodiments and efficient adaptation to downstream tasks. We introduce Rho, a family of open-weights VLA models for bimanual manipulation designed for data-light task adaptation on 3 embodiments representative of dual-arm robots across research labs and the industry -- YAM Box, UR AI Trainer, and FR3 Duo. We systematically ablate Rho's action-expert architecture and training recipe, and show in controlled simulation and physical-robot experiments that embodiment midtraining improves downstream adaptation. The resulting Rho variants for YAM Box, UR AI Trainer, and FR3 Duo match or outperform existing open-weights VLAs and achieve the strongest overall performance across the tasks, embodiments, and baselines evaluated in this report. We further demonstrate the Rho model family's built-in capacity for online adaptation: an internal latent policy learns from corrective feedback to select observation-conditioned noise inputs for the frozen flow-matching action expert. With as few as 15 corrected episodes, adapting this lightweight module enables Rho to handle task situations at the fringe of its offline finetuning distribution. Together, these results position Rho as both a strong general-purpose robotic manipulation model and a practical foundation for adaptation. We release the base Rho model and the embodiment-specific checkpoints to facilitate Rho's deployment in research experiments and practical industrial use cases.

papers.title_en: Directed Temporal Representations for Offline Visual Control
papers.authors: Chenyang Yuan, Haoyu Wang, Zhuo Sun, Xiaoyuan Cheng
papers.evidence: 面向离线视觉控制的世界模型潜在几何
papers.tldr: 离线视觉控制中，预测式世界模型虽能提供紧凑表征，但其潜在几何偏向预测相似性，未必对齐控制所需的时间可达性。DTRC 在冻结的 LeWorldModel 特征上，从离线视觉轨迹学习有向时间准度量，并用短程偏移校准距离、自举目标扩展长时可达、动作条件一致性对齐局部动态。该距离表征时间到达代价，其变化给出目标相对时间进度，可作为时间评论家直接训练目标条件策略。在十个视觉控制任务上，DTRC 优于规划与直接策略基线，并在四个 LeWM 任务上验证了短程校准、长程方向结构及正向转移进度。
papers.abstract_en: Predictive world models provide compact visual representations for control. Control requires a latent geometry aligned with temporal reachability rather than predictive similarity alone. We introduce Directed Temporal Representations for Control (DTRC), which learns such a geometry from offline visual trajectories on top of frozen LeWorldModel (LeWM) features. DTRC constructs a directed temporal quasimetric over the learned control representation. Short-range temporal offsets calibrate the distance scale. Bootstrapped targets extend temporal reachability across longer horizons. Action-conditioned consistency aligns the representation with local transition dynamics. The resulting distance estimates temporal reaching cost, and its change across a transition defines goal-relative temporal progress. We use this progress signal as a temporal critic for direct goal-conditioned policy learning. Model-assisted targets provide an additional training-time refinement under behavior-support and dynamics-agreement constraints. Across ten visual control tasks, DTRC achieves strong goal-conditioned control performance relative to planning and direct-policy baselines. Held-out diagnostics on the four LeWM tasks show consistent short-range temporal calibration, task-dependent long-range and directional structure, and positive transition-level progress. Temporal supervision improves the same flow-policy parameterization across all four LeWM tasks, while the resulting policy acts directly without iterative trajectory search at test time.

papers.title_en: Event-Aligned Visual Action Reasoning for World Action Models
papers.authors: Xiaomeng Yang, Yushu Wu, Yi Gao, Yuhao Lei, Xuan Zhang, Pu Zhao, Yanzhi Wang
papers.evidence: 面向世界-动作模型的事件对齐视觉动作推理
papers.tldr: 现有World-Action Models按预设时间间隔组织视觉想象，忽略任务关键交互与连接过渡的不同作用。本文提出事件对齐视觉动作推理框架，围绕交互事件组织视觉-动作预测，并按交互动态调整推理粒度。在DOMINO成功率较基线提升10.26个百分点，并在RoboTwin 2.0上表现有竞争力，且无需目标层级适配即可从Level 1迁移到Level 2和3。
papers.abstract_en: World-Action Models (WAMs) utilize future visual prediction as an intermediate reasoning process to guide action generation. However, existing WAMs typically structure visual imagination according to predefined temporal intervals, without explicitly accounting for the different roles of task-critical interactions and connecting transitions. We argue that effective visual foresight should align directly with task-relevant interactions and their corresponding reasoning demands. To this end, we introduce an event-aligned visual action reasoning framework that organizes visual-action prediction around interaction events. Through event-aligned visual-action supervision, WAM learns to generate event-aligned visual context in each imagined rollout, placing greater emphasis on critical state changes that inform action generation. This shapes the visual reasoning granularity according to the underlying interaction dynamics, with detailed reasoning around task-critical events and coarser progression through connecting transitions. Furthermore, we introduce an execution validity head that identifies the valid portion of each predicted action sequence, avoiding redundant actions during chunked inference. Experiments demonstrate a 10.26 percentage point improvement in DOMINO success rate over baseline and competitive performance on RoboTwin 2.0. It also transfers from DOMINO Level 1 to Levels 2 and 3 without target-level adaptation.

papers.title_en: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments
papers.authors: Zhiqin Yang, Chenxin Li, Xiaomeng Hu, Yibin Liu, Weidong Huang, Jiankai Sun, Haitao Li, Zijian Wu, Yuzhi Huang, Fanding Huang, Hanwen Sun, Jiashun Liu, Jingqi Tong, Mingxin Huang, Shaoli Hu, Shijue Huang, Tianyi Bai, Xinyuan Wang, Yunlong Lin, Zhengyang Tang, Zhexin Zhang, Zhuo Chen, Xierui Song, Juntao Dai, Boyuan Chen, Jiaming Ji, Fangneng Zhan, Mengkang Hu, Wei Xue, Yonggang Zhang, Han Hu, Tsung-Yi Ho, Yike Guo
papers.evidence: 覆盖操作、运动、驾驶的机器人使用仿真基准
papers.tldr: 通用智能体能否将数字工具能力迁移到物理世界仍不明确。本文提出 RobotWorld 仿真基准，通过机器人接口把指令与观测转为物理执行，覆盖操作、移动操作、运动、驾驶和空中控制等 84 项任务，并设交互预算与成功检查。联合分析结果与轨迹发现，智能体能搭建分割、标定、空间估计和动力学计算等流程，却常因状态丢失、不会纠错、恢复过晚或误判完成而失败，且模型间迁移不均衡。该基准为训练更可靠的物理世界智能体提供了试验场与能力缺口清单。
papers.abstract_en: General-purpose agents increasingly write code, use tools, and complete complex digital tasks, raising the question of how far these capabilities carry into the physical world. To investigate this, we introduce RobotWorld, a challenging simulation testbed for robot use: turning instructions and observations into physical task execution through robot interfaces. Its 84 tasks span manipulation, mobile manipulation, locomotion, driving, and aerial control, with explicit interaction budgets and executable success checks. By analysing task outcomes alongside execution traces, we identify both the capabilities that transfer and the gaps that prevent reliable completion. Furthermore, we find that current agents can construct sophisticated perception and control workflows, including image segmentation, camera calibration, spatial estimation, and dynamics-based computation. These capabilities, however, do not consistently compose into successful behaviour: agents lose task-relevant object states despite reaching commanded poses, fail to correct ineffective actions, recover too late, or mistake unfinished tasks for completion. This uneven transfer also differs across models: Astra succeeds more often on spatial and constrained-contact goals, whereas Opus 5.5 succeeds more often on continuous-balance and timed-interaction goals. By linking these outcomes to execution behaviour, RobotWorld provides both a rigorous proving ground and an empirical account of the remaining capability gaps, thereby establishing concrete targets for training and designing more reliable physical-world agents.

papers.title_en: FOCUS: From Privileged States to RGB-D with Controlled Modality Switching and Representation Alignment
papers.authors: Filip Grigorov, Kourosh Darvish, Nandita Vijaykumar
papers.evidence: 面向机器人操作任务的视觉强化学习PPO框架
papers.tldr: 视觉机器人操作强化学习因RGB-D观测高维含噪而样本效率低；仿真特权状态可加速训练，但测试时缺失造成模态鸿沟。FOCUS是单阶段PPO框架：评论家利用特权状态，并按两模态动作分布的KL散度自动调节演员从RGB-D或特权潜变量采集rollout，同时对齐表征。五类任务上，平均测试成功率由0.71升至0.93，预算归一化AUC由0.47升至0.65；Pick-and-Place成功率由0.47升至0.86，AUC由0.12升至0.61。机制弥合模态差距，提升效率。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-based reinforcement learning for robotic manipulation is sample-inefficient because RGB-D observations are high-dimensional and noisy. Privileged state information available in simulation can accelerate training, but its absence at test time creates a train-test modality gap. We propose FOCUS, a single-stage PPO framework that trains the critic on privileged state while automatically regulating whether the actor collects rollouts from RGB-D or privileged-state latents. Regulation is driven by the KL divergence between the action distributions induced by the two modalities, while representation alignment encourages consistent action selection across them. Together, these mechanisms limit RGB-D rollouts when the actor's action distributions from RGB-D and privileged-state latents disagree. As they align, RGB-D exposure increases, shifting on-policy training toward the RGB-D inputs used at test time. Across five manipulation tasks, FOCUS raises average test success from 0.71 to 0.93 relative to the strongest RGB-D-at-test baseline on each task. When accounting for each method's complete training pipeline, budget-normalized training-success AUC increases from 0.47 to 0.65. On Pick-and-Place, test success rises from 0.47 to 0.86, while AUC increases from 0.12 to 0.61, a 5.0x improvement in learning efficiency over the fixed interaction budget.

papers.title_en: Transferable Spatial Temporal Coherence Adversarial Attack on Black-Box Vision Language Models for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Heyam Bin Jahlan Areej Alhothali Abeer Alhothali
papers.evidence: 针对自动驾驶场景黑盒视觉语言模型的对抗攻击
papers.tldr: 面向自动驾驶的黑盒视觉语言模型（VLM）视频对抗鲁棒性仍待探索。本文提出可迁移时空连贯性对抗攻击STCA，通过字幕引导选帧、空间扰动与运动掩码破坏跨帧时序连贯。在BDD100K和nuScenes上对Video LLaVA-7B、Qwen2.5-VL-7B与Dolphin测试，空间攻击以高SSIM取得高ASR。结果表明现有VLM在驾驶场景下极易受攻击，凸显鲁棒防御需求。
papers.abstract_en: The rapid integration of Vision Language Models (VLMs) into sensitive systems introduces critical safety vulnerabilities that remain unexplored in exist studies. While adversarial attack robustness has been extensively studied for image-based models, the susceptibility of VLMs to temporally-aware adversarial attacks against video in driving context poses a distinct and under examined threat. In this paper, we introduce novel adversarial attack against video targeting VLM models used for autonomous driving scenes named Spatial Temporal Coherence Adversarial Attack (STCA). Our attack comprise from three stages: modalities expansion, Spatial attack, and STCA attack. In modalities expansion, we propose caption-guided frame selection method in order to ensure that adversarial perturbation target the most semantically significant frames. Secondly.In spatial attack, we craft effective perturbation and preserve high similarity. Then the perturbed video generated fed into STCA stage that disrupt cross-frame temporal coherence using motion guided mask. Our method operate under black box threat model against victim target VLMs, relying solely on transferability from white-box surrogate model.We conduct our experiments on the BDD100K and nuScenes autonomous driving datasets across three VLM models: Video LLaVA-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and Dolphin. Experimental results demonstrate spatial attack achieves an ASR with high SSIM. Our finding reveal that existing video language model, remain highly susceptible to adversarial attack in autonomous driving scenarios, underscoring the urgent need for robust defense for VLM models.

papers.title_en: iAm.md: Robot Skill Self-Assessment through Agentic Introspection for Unknown Open-Vocabulary Domains
papers.authors: Vincenzo Guarino, Emanuele Musumeci, Vincenzo Suriani, Daniele Nardi
papers.evidence: 面向具身任务的智能体式机器人技能自评估
papers.tldr: 基于大语言模型的具身智能体虽能生成看似合理的机器人规划，却常因上下文限制或幻觉出现“接地失败”，即未验证机器人与环境是否支持所请求操作。本文提出iAm.md，一种Markdown标准与生成框架，将机器人行为生成建模为代码生成，并通过开放词汇语义建图，把视觉语言检测与物体分割关联到持久物体记录，实现智能体内省。在仿真TIAGo的导航与操作任务中，该标准化表示同时支持技能自评估与可执行任务泛化，为未知开放词汇域提供机器人技能自评估机制。
papers.abstract_en: Agentic AI based on Large Language Model generalization capabilities offers a wide range of potential applications, including planning for embodied tasks. For example, embodied agents based on Foundation models can generate plausible plans in autonomous robotics scenarios. Due to limited context windows or hallucinatory phenomena in the next-token prediction formulation, behaviors may be generated without establishing whether the deployed robot and the observed environment actually support the requested operation, in what we call a "grounding failure". Thanks to the recent improvements in reasoning capabilities of foundation models, autonomous robot behavior generation problem can be formulated as a code generation problem. We present iAm.md, a Markdown standard and generation framework, that allows anchoring this process in complementary forms of deployment evidence. Through open-vocabulary semantic mapping, we combine local vision-language detections and object segmentation and refer them to persistent object records in this intermediate standardized representation, allowing agentic introspection. We then study this new technique on a simulated TIAGo, on navigation-and-manipulation tasks, showing how this standardized representation jointly supports skill self-assessment and executable task generalization.

papers.title_en: Towards Path-Creative Navigation: Robot Navigation through Embodied Interaction
papers.authors: Haoyu Xi, Siwei Cheng, Xiangyuan Liu, Brenda Li, Wei Zhang
papers.evidence: 机器人通过具身交互导航并恢复可通行空间
papers.tldr: 传统导航在杂乱受限环境中假设环境固定，仅在既有自由空间内寻路，遇到可动结构、物体或行人时难以抵达目标。本文提出 Path-Creative Navigation（PCN），让机器人通过协调移动与具身交互恢复自由空间，并构建无地图导航框架。该框架融合视觉、LiDAR 与里程计，利用可通行性决策判断阻塞能否处理与安全绕行，按需推动关节结构、移动物体、避障或请求行人让路。仿真与两个真实任务显示，其任务完成率优于基线，体现移动与交互协同的贡献。
papers.abstract_en: Autonomous navigation in cluttered and constrained environments typically assumes a fixed environment and searches only for paths within existing free space. However, a route can be blocked by an articulated structure, a movable object, or a pedestrian, and reaching the goal may therefore require appropriate embodied interaction with the environment. This paper formulates Path-Creative Navigation (PCN), a navigation paradigm in which the robot recovers free space by coordinating locomotion and embodied interaction, and addresses one class of PCN tasks with a mapless framework. The vision-LiDAR-odometry framework integrates local observations, obstacle geometry, and robot-state estimates through a unified navigation system, providing stable semantic and geometric information for navigation and interaction. The traversability-aware decision method utilizes visual and LiDAR distance information to determine whether a blockage is actionable and whether it can be safely bypassed, enabling the robot to interact only when necessary while supporting articulated structure pushing, movable object pushing, obstacle avoidance, and pedestrian requests. We design simulation scenarios and evaluate different methods in both simulation and two real-world tasks that cannot be completed by conventional navigation alone without embodied interaction. These results demonstrate that our framework achieves higher task completion than the baseline methods by coordinating navigation and interaction in cluttered and constrained environments.

papers.title_en: Akule: Fast and Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Sparse Interaction Diffusion
papers.authors: Manav Vora, Gokul Puthumanaillam, Aditya Penumarti, Jane Shin, Melkior Ornik
papers.evidence: 基于稀疏交互扩散的多机器人运动规划
papers.tldr: 多机器人运动规划中扩散模型先验表达力强，但大规模协同需避免昂贵联合计算。Akule提出稀疏交互扩散框架，在冻结单机器人先验上学习成对修正Rφ、上下文选择器Uψ与组合器Gω，将哪些交互值得计算与如何组合效果分离。联合提议交由下游搜索规划器验证修复，在多个基准上实现最高25倍完整规划器加速、零样本群体迁移及256机器人规划。该工作以可扩展稀疏交互分解提升多机器人规划效率与规模。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion models provide expressive trajectory priors for multi-robot motion planning (MRMP), but scaling them to large teams requires coordinating individual motions without expensive joint computation. We introduce Akule, a sparse interaction diffusion framework that augments a frozen single-robot prior with three learned modules: a reusable pairwise correction model $R_φ$, a contextual selector $U_ψ$ that determines which corrections to evaluate, and a composer $G_ω$ that combines their effects through context-dependent signed weights. This decomposition separates which interactions merit computation from how their effects should be combined into coordinated denoising updates. We train $R_φ$ using matched pairwise trajectory optimizations, then learn $G_ω$ and $U_ψ$ from physically optimized joint trajectories without requiring a prescribed ground-truth interaction graph. The resulting joint proposals are passed to a downstream search-based planner for validation and repair. Across diverse MRMP benchmarks, Akule achieves competitive planning success, complete-planner speedups of up to $25\times$, zero-shot population transfer, and successful planning with up to $256$ robots. Ablations further demonstrate that learned selection and composition reduce pre-repair conflicts and downstream repair effort relative to heuristic selection and uniform summation.
